answer: Agents can make high-value trades conditional on a bond locked in a shared ledger, with the bond forfeited when counterparties prove an agent double-spent or violated a signed contract. A newcomer must earn trust through small, settled transactions before accessing larger credit, so spawning identities does not multiply buying power. The attacker must fund each identity separately and risks losing its bond; copper delivered at a wharf or produce from a garden can start the same costly reputation trail.
